response.message: We're building an anomaly-detection pipeline for synthetic sensor events on IBM Cloud. I've sketched it as IBM Event Streams for ingestion and buffering, then a Code Engine validator, a watsonx.ai model and a PostgreSQL results store, with alerts sent through Event Notifications. The first local test would replay a fixture of good events plus bad ones (unknown device, wrong units, duplicates, late and out-of-order events) through the validator with a mocked model. That checks the pipeline logic, not detection quality: we'd still need to validate a real model on held-out synthetic data and record its false-alarm rate. Nothing has been deployed, and no region or account access is approved yet. How late can an event arrive and still be scored? For example, "up to 5 minutes late gets scored, anything later is rejected with a reason."

proposal.title: IBM sensor anomaly pipeline – first concrete sketch
proposal.body: Scope: synthetic sensor events through ingestion, durable buffering, validation, inference, results and operator alerting on IBM Cloud. Assumptions: the region is still to be selected, and the model is mocked in the local test and remains unvalidated. Event Streams keeps raw topics for replay and a reject topic for failed events. Neither IBM Terraform generation nor any deployment is covered or verified.

data.label: Synthetic device publisher
data.description: An external test publisher sends synthetic telemetry: device_id, event_id, timestamp, value and unit. It sits outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Telemetry buffer
data.description: A Kafka topic (telemetry.raw) keyed by device_id keeps order per device. Retention allows replay after a disconnect, and consumers resume from committed offsets. A telemetry.rejected topic holds invalid events with a reason.

data.label: Validator & scoring app
data.description: Consumer app. It rejects unknown devices and invalid units, keeping device identity, timestamps and units unchanged. It drops duplicates by device_id + event_id and applies the explicit late/out-of-order window. It then calls the model, writes an idempotent result and raises alerts.

data.label: Device registry
data.description: Lists known device IDs and the units allowed for each sensor. It is read by the validator.

data.label: Anomaly model
data.description: Deployed anomaly model that returns a score, evidence features and a model version. It is mocked in the local test, and its real quality is unvalidated.

data.label: Anomaly results
data.description: Stores results with a unique key (device_id, event_id), so a duplicate event gives one result. Each result records the evidence and model version.

data.label: Operator alert
data.description: Sends anomaly alerts that name the device, evidence and model version to the operator destination.

data.label: Operator
data.description: The person who receives and triages anomaly alerts.

data.label: Pipeline monitoring
data.description: Tracks consumer lag, reject counts, duplicates dropped, late events and model latency.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Stops bad data from producing false anomalies.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Reject unknown device and invalid units"
requirementDrafts.statement: Events from unknown devices or with invalid units are rejected with a reason and never scored.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prevents repeated alerts and double counting.
requirementDrafts.statement: Duplicate events (same device_id and event_id) produce exactly one result.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without a policy, results can't be reproduced.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Late and out-of-order telemetry follows an explicit policy"
requirementDrafts.statement: Late and out-of-order telemetry is handled by an explicit, documented window. The window length is still open.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Ensures recovery doesn't lose data or create duplicates.
requirementDrafts.statement: After a disconnect, processing resumes by replaying from committed Event Streams offsets without losing events.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Lets operators audit and trust alerts.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Anomaly output names evidence and model version"
requirementDrafts.statement: Each anomaly result and alert names its evidence and model version, and preserves device identity, timestamps and units.

response.message:
Here's where things stand: no runtime checks ran, so the design isn't validated yet, and the empty failures list doesn't mean it's correct. Every blocker comes from the same cause. None of the IBM pieces (Event Streams, Code Engine, Cloudant, watsonx.ai, PostgreSQL, Event Notifications) has a supported generator contract. The only IBM contract available is private object storage, and switching to it would shrink this pipeline down to storage.

So the fix isn't a diagram change. It needs product engineering: a native Event Streams/Code Engine implementation that can reproduce this artifact (digest 5c94f945…, revision 2). The two existing systems (the synthetic publisher and the operator) also each need a plan for how they connect into the pipeline.

Meanwhile, we can close a design decision those tests will need. How late can an event arrive and still be scored, for example "up to 5 minutes late, anything later is rejected with a reason"?
